_meta.purpose: Sitemap <lastmod> and JSON-LD dateModified source for the cloud-rest-api tag and schema pages (content-adapter-generated, no honest per-page date otherwise available).
_meta.methodology: Each tag/schema key is hashed (sha256 of canonical JSON: the sorted list of [path, method, operation] triples for a tag, or the schema object itself). A key's lastmod is set/updated to the run date only when its hash differs from the previously recorded hash (i.e. a real content change was observed), or when the key is newly seen. A key with no lastmod means no change has been observed since this ledger started tracking it on the seeded_at date below -- never infer or backfill an earlier date without direct evidence, since an inaccurate site-wide lastmod stamp gets Google's Search Console to distrust lastmod values across the whole sitemap. A one-time historical backfill (see _meta.backfill) extended this ledger using archived captures of the spec itself as direct evidence of when tracked content changed.
_meta.seed_note: Seeded from a single live-spec snapshot only. Historical Wayback Machine snapshots (2026-03-04, 2026-05-13, 2026-08-02) exist for this endpoint but could not be fetched in this run (persistent HTTP 429 from web.archive.org). No lastmod dates were assigned on the seed pass; every tag/schema starts with a hash and no date, and will get an honest lastmod the first time the nightly job observes a hash change. Update (2026-08-25): retried, and the Wayback CDX API returned HTTP 200 with no rate-limiting this time. The three snapshots below were fetched and used for the one-time backfill recorded in _meta.backfill.

observations.source: git commit 34820a4bcc (this ledger's own dateless seed -- a direct observation of the spec at seed time)

backfill.method: Walk observations oldest to newest. Record a change event when, relative to the immediately preceding observation in which the key was seen, the key's hash differs (content changed) or the key was absent in the preceding observation and present now (content created in that window). Set lastmod to the date of the latest such event. Keys present in the oldest observation with no later event, or absent from every observation, stay dateless.
backfill.precision: A stamped date is the date on which the changed content was directly observed, not necessarily the date the change was made. The true change falls somewhere in the interval after the preceding observation up to and including the stamped date (up to 70 days before 2026-05-13, up to 81 days before 2026-08-02, up to 13 days before 2026-08-15). The later, more recent bound of each interval is what gets stamped, so no page ever claims to be fresher than a date on which its current content was actually observed.
backfill.coverage: 318 of 819 previously dateless keys recovered a lastmod; the remainder had not changed since the oldest available observation (2026-03-04) and legitimately stay dateless.
backfill.not_overwritten: No pre-existing lastmod value (all set by the live nightly job since 2026-08-19) was read, compared, or modified by this backfill.
